audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL transaction processing (Cancun transactions, gas repricing, precompiles, DAO fork), CL beacon chain operations (Deneb blob commitments, attestations, voluntary exits, validator activation), CL-EL interfaces (Engine API), P2P discovery (ENR), wallet RPC interfaces (batch calls, block queries), and BLS credential management.

in_scope: State Transitions (DAO fork, Istanbul, Tangerine Whistle)

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EVM component invoking precompiles; not an external entity. The actual external entity is the transaction sender or smart contract originating the call.
Internal data representation within the EVM, not an external entity. Calldata originates from external transaction sources.
Internal EVM state tracking gas availability. Not an external source of data.
SELFDESTRUCT beneficiary is an address parameter, not an entity that sends data into the system. The entity providing this parameter is the contract execution context.
The signer is represented by the cryptographic signature embedded in the transaction. The actual external entity is the transaction source (user/peer).

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit transactions and query block data via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. All input is potentially malicious: malformed transactions, resource exhaustion attempts, invalid parameters.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via Wallet RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps submit batched call requests via wallet RPC. No authentication on the DApp side; malicious DApps could submit invalid flow control parameters, exploit atomicity guarantees, or attempt resource exhaustion.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P (EL)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. They can send invalid blocks, malformed transactions, attempt eclipse attacks, or propagate blocks with incorrect gas calculations or missing fork markers.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P (CL)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip (BLSToExecutionChange messages, attestations, beacon blocks)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL P2P peers are unauthenticated. They can send conflicting BLSToExecutionChange messages, invalid attestations, or malicious beacon blocks with incorrect blob commitments.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer via P2P (CL)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon block gossip (blob KZG commitments, execution payloads)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block proposers are validators but their blocks are untrusted until validated. Proposers may include invalid blob commitments, incorrect versioned hashes, or malformed execution payloads.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT shared secret. The CL is a trusted component, but payload content (execution payloads, versioned hashes, parent beacon block root) must still be validated by the EL. A compromised or buggy CL could send invalid payloads.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API responses (payload validation results, blob gas metrics)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT. The EL provides payload validity status and blob gas accounting back to the CL. Content must be validated: incorrect blob_gas_used or excess_blob_gas could corrupt beacon state.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator via Beacon API / P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: BLSToExecutionChange submission, voluntary exit submission, attestation submission
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators submit signed messages but are untrusted. They may submit conflicting withdrawal credential changes, invalid exit signatures, or try to exploit the extended attestation inclusion window.

trusted_external_entities.name: Smart Contract via EVM CALL
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Smart contracts invoke precompiles with arbitrary calldata. Malicious contracts may supply invalid field elements, points not on curve, points not in subgroup, or attempt gas exhaustion via large MSM/pairing inputs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via Discovery Protocol
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Discovery protocol peers are unauthenticated. They may attempt amplification attacks via ENRRequest without prior ping exchange, send forged ENR records, or manipulate sequence numbers.

trusted_external_entities.name: Node Operator via Local Configuration
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Local broadcast file loading (BLSToExecutionChange broadcast file)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Node operators load broadcast files locally. While they have local system access (semi-trusted channel), the file content originates from a community repository and must be validated. Malicious or corrupt broadcast files could cause rejection of legitimate messages.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: decode transaction type, verify signature bounds (r, s within SECP256K1 curve order), recover sender, validate gas sufficiency, check nonce overflow (< 2^64-1), enforce init code size limit (MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE), and compute intrinsic gas costs.
Block number parameter must be validated. baseFee field inclusion must be conditional on fork status. Response must not leak internal state beyond what is publicly available.

Flow control parameters must be validated: schema validation, capability scope checks, rollback-none atomicity conflict detection. Wallet must correctly implement requested atomicity and failure handling semantics.

Full block validation required: header validation (number, timestamp, gas, difficulty, parent hash), fork-specific checks (DAO extra data marker in 10-block window), gas cost enforcement per fork rules (Istanbul, Tangerine Whistle repricing), 63/64 call gas allocation.

Messages must be checked against broadcast file if loaded. Conflicting messages (different signature for same validator) must be rejected. Messages for unknown validators must be accepted normally. BLS signature verification required.

Blob KZG commitment count must be <= MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK (6). Versioned hashes must be validated against execution payload blob transactions via is_valid_versioned_hashes. Execution payload must be forwarded to EL via Engine API for validation.

JWT authentication must be verified. Execution payload content must be fully validated: versioned hash consistency with blob commitments, parent beacon block root correctness, blob gas metrics accuracy. The EL must not blindly trust CL-provided payload data.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Engine API response (VALID/INVALID status, blob gas values)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: JWT authentication must be verified. CL must handle both VALID and INVALID responses correctly. blob_gas_used and excess_blob_gas values cached in beacon state header must be validated for consistency.

BLS signatures must be cryptographically verified. Voluntary exits must use fixed CAPELLA_FORK_VERSION domain for signature validation (EIP-7044). Validator index must be active. Only one BLSToExecutionChange per validator. Attestation inclusion window must respect MIN_ATTESTATION_INCLUSION_DELAY and extended epoch rules (EIP-7045).

Input validation required: input length check, Fp/Fp2 field element encoding (top 16 bytes zero, value < modulus), point-on-curve verification, subgroup membership for MSM/pairing. Gas must be correctly computed (fixed for ADD/MAP, variable with discount for MSM, linear for pairing). All validation failures must consume all provided gas.

ENRRequest must be rejected if no prior ping exchange exists (amplification attack prevention). Request expiration timestamp must be in the future. ENRResponse signature must be verified via secp256k1. Request hash must match pending request. ENR sequence numbers in ping/pong must be correctly compared.

Broadcast file content must be validated: BLS signatures must be verified for each entry, validator indices must correspond to active validators. File integrity should be verified before loading. Conflicting entries in the file should be detected.
